question: In the study of clinical resistance to RAF inhibition in metastatic melanoma, what percentage of the cohort had resistance alterations in MAPK-pathway genes?
gold_notes: 44.4% (20/45) had MAPK-pathway resistance alterations; MAP2K2 (MEK2) nominated as a new resistance gene.

## Answer

In the study of clinical resistance to RAF inhibition in metastatic melanoma by [Van Allen et al.](papers/24265153.html), **44.4% (20 out of 45 patients)** of the cohort had resistance alterations in MAPK-pathway genes, including [NRAS](genes/NRAS.html), [BRAF](genes/BRAF.html) amplification, [MAP2K1](genes/MAP2K1.html), [MAP2K2](genes/MAP2K2.html), [MITF](genes/MITF.html), and [NF1](genes/NF1.html).

More broadly, genetic alterations in known or putative RAF inhibitor resistance genes were observed in **51% (23 of 45 patients)** overall, which included additional alterations beyond the core MAPK pathway.
